newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian truck sales fell 11.6 percent in January.
newsitem.headline: Italian truck sales fell 11.6 percent in January.

text.p: Italian truck sales in January dipped 11.58 percent to 10,791 compared to 12,204 in January 1996, according to vehicle making association Anfia and importing body Unrae.
Italian makers of commercial vehicles saw their share of the market fall to 58.81 percent, or 6,346 trucks in January, compared to a 59.05 percent share in January 1996.

Among truck makers, Piaggio sales rose 21 percent to 418 vehicles to take a 3.87 percent share of the market. But Fiat's heavy truck division Iveco saw a sales fall of 22.9 percent to 1,398 vehicles sold, while Fiat Auto sales fell 9.5 percent to 4,494 trucks.

Among imported trucks, Ford was in first place with a 10.86 percent share of the market, but saw sales slip 27.7 percent to 1,172 vehicles. In second place was Nissan with a 5.81 percent market share, but it saw sales fall 25 percent to 627 vehicles.
Renault had a 5.1 percent market share with 550 vehicles, but saw sales dip 32.9 percent, while Volkswagen's market share increased to 3.28 percent as sales rose 25.5 percent from year ago levels.
